subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Uterine leiomyomas: FIGO classification, medical management, myomectomy and adenomyosis

steps.tx: Uterine leiomyomas are the most frequent benign pelvic neoplasms in women, with a cumulative lifetime incidence exceeding seventy percent. Originating from monoclonal transformation of smooth muscle cells, their growth is strictly dependent on estrogen and progesterone. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics categorizes fibroids using the **FIGO classification system**, scoring locations from Type 0 entirely intracavitary to Type 7 pedunculated subserosal.
steps.say: Uterine leiomyomas are common benign smooth muscle tumors dependent on estrogen and progesterone. FIGO classifies fibroids from Type zero, which is entirely inside the uterine cavity, through Type seven, which is pedunculated subserosal.

steps.tx: Medical management of symptomatic fibroids aims to control heavy menstrual bleeding and reduce tumor volume prior to definitive surgery. Short-term therapy with **GnRH agonists** (such as leuprolide or goserelin) downregulates pituitary GnRH receptors, inducing profound hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. This chemical menopause decreases leiomyoma volume by thirty to fifty percent within three months and corrects chronic iron deficiency anemia before planned myomectomy.
steps.say: Medical therapy controls heavy bleeding and shrinks fibroids before surgery. GnRH agonists induce a temporary chemical menopause, shrinking fibroid volume by thirty to fifty percent within three months and correcting iron deficiency anemia.

left.title: Medical management of fibroids
points: GnRH agonists: shrinks volume by 30-50% preoperatively
52 mg LNG-IUS: controls menorrhagia in non-cavity distorting fibroids
Tranexamic acid: non-hormonal blood loss reduction during menses
Selective progesterone receptor modulators: variable availability

right.title: Procedural and surgical options
points: Hysteroscopic myomectomy: for FIGO Types 0, 1 and selected 2
Uterine artery embolization (UAE): for completed childbearing
Hysterectomy: definitive cure for symptomatic women

steps.tx: A critical clinical entity frequently co-existing with fibroids is **adenomyosis**, defined as the non-neoplastic presence of heterotopic endometrial glands and stroma embedded deep within the myometrium. This ectopic tissue provokes reactive hyperplastic hypertrophy of surrounding myometrial smooth muscle. Patients characteristically present with progressively severe secondary dysmenorrhea, heavy prolonged menstrual bleeding, and a diffusely enlarged, tender, globular uterus.
steps.say: Adenomyosis occurs when endometrial glands grow deep within the uterine muscle, causing muscle hypertrophy. Patients experience progressively severe period pain, heavy bleeding, and a tender, symmetrically enlarged, boggy uterus on examination.

steps.tx: Magnetic resonance imaging represents the non-invasive gold standard for the definitive diagnosis of adenomyosis. T2-weighted pelvic MRI characteristically demonstrates diffuse or focal widening of the myometrial **junctional zone**, with a maximal thickness exceeding twelve millimeters considered pathognomonic. First-line medical therapy mirrors that of endometriosis, utilizing the 52-milligram levonorgestrel intrauterine system, while hysterectomy provides definitive surgical cure.
steps.say: Pelvic MRI is the gold standard for diagnosing adenomyosis. T2 images demonstrate thickening of the junctional zone exceeding twelve millimeters. First-line medical treatment is the levonorgestrel intrauterine system, while hysterectomy provides definitive cure.
